top5.title: SEC investigates Nvidia’s accounting
top5.description: The U.S. SEC has opened a civil investigation to determine whether Nvidia misled investors about its accounting, without currently accusing the company of breaking the law. The investigation focuses in part on its sales to Singapore and on a customer suspected of rerouting chips to China.
top5.why: The SEC’s investigation into Nvidia’s accounting and possible chip rerouting to China could materially affect the AI leader’s valuation, disclosures and export-control exposure.

top5.title: Trump threatens to tax data centers built overseas
top5.description: Donald Trump said U.S. companies would be prohibited from building data centers overseas or would have to pay a very high tax. Alphabet, Amazon, Microsoft, Meta and Oracle already have data centers in other countries.
top5.why: Trump’s threat to tax or prohibit overseas data centers could reshape the global infrastructure strategies and capital spending of America’s largest technology companies.

top5.title: SoftBank chief explored a $1 trillion takeover of SK Hynix
top5.description: Masayoshi Son, SoftBank’s chief, explored a $1 trillion takeover of SK Hynix, according to The Information.
top5.why: SoftBank’s reported exploration of a $1 trillion takeover of SK Hynix highlights the strategic and financial stakes surrounding control of advanced memory for AI systems.

top5.title: YouTube nears $3 billion settlement with U.S. schools
top5.description: YouTube is close to a settlement worth up to $3 billion with school districts accusing it of designing an addictive platform. The settlement would also include new protections, though details have not yet been specified.
top5.why: A potential $3 billion YouTube settlement with U.S. schools could establish a major financial and regulatory precedent for platform design, child safety and addiction claims.

top5.title: Gemini can now handle multistep everyday tasks
top5.description: Google has expanded Gemini’s Tasks mode to perform tasks such as scheduling appointments, reviewing bills and placing grocery orders. The service asks for confirmation before certain critical steps, but Google recommends checking the results.
top5.why: Google’s expansion of Gemini into multistep tasks such as booking appointments, reviewing bills and ordering groceries signals a shift from chatbots toward agentic consumer automation.
